email.subject1: signal to action latency at Fello
email.body1:
Rick, saw Fello is launching Felix, the AI agent that qualifies and hands off leads live.

With volume like that, the real bottleneck on the revenue side is signal-to-action latency, how fast a buying signal turns into a booked meeting. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep, every touch auto-logged.

I built a personalized signal play for Fello off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Rick, quick follow-up for Fello.

Most RevOps leaders find their measurable lift sits in the gap between signal captured and rep action, not in adding more activity. That latency quietly caps pipeline no matter how clean the data is.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound motion, three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent. I'll bring specifics for Fello.
email.body3:
Rick, last bit of proof for Fello.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Fello's reply rate likely compares to other growth-stage startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Rick, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action latency without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Right before a product launch, I know the RevOps stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Fello either way.
